chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

My father عليه السلام used to say: There is nothing more corrupting to the heart than a sin. Indeed, the heart commits the sin, and it continues with it until it overcomes it, and turns its upper part into its lower.

key_terms.أَسْفَلَهُ: its lower part, symbolizing inversion and corruption
key_terms.أَعْلَاهُ: its upper part, symbolizing its proper elevated state
key_terms.الْقَلْبِ: the spiritual heart, the inner faculty of moral and spiritual perception
key_terms.خَطِيئَةٍ: a sin or offense that corrupts the soul

ai.seo_question: How do sins affect the heart in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that sin is the most destructive force for the heart, gradually overpowering it when it is repeatedly committed. It depicts spiritual corruption as an inward inversion, where the heart’s proper state is overturned through persistence in wrongdoing.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Talha Bin Zayd, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘There is none from the things which is more spoiling for the heart than a sin. If the heart falls for the sin, so it (the sin) does not cease to be with it until it overcomes it (the heart), and its upper part comes to be its lower’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Talhah ibn Zayd from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
My father would say, ‘There is nothing more destructive to the heart than sins. The heart falls on sins and remains that way until sins subdue it and then it turns upside down.’”
